summary:
The "Energy Threat Analysis Center Act of 2026" (H.R. 7305, 119th Congress) amends Section 40125(c) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (codified at 42 U.S.C. 18724(c)) to reauthorize and expand the Department of Energy's Energy Sector Operational Support for Cyberresilience Program. As reported by the Committee on Energy and Commerce, the bill strikes all text after the enacting clause and substitutes an amended version.

The operative mechanism is a series of amendments to Section 40125(c). Section 2(1) restructures paragraph (1)'s enumerated program purposes: it redesignates existing subparagraphs (A) through (E) as (B) through (F), and inserts a new subparagraph (A) establishing purposes directed at strengthening the collective defense, response, and resilience of the U.S. energy sector—through enhanced government-industry collaboration (classified and unclassified information exchange, collective threat analysis, and establishment of technical infrastructure for advanced analytics), advancing understanding of national security risks and vulnerabilities, and increasing sector understanding of threat actor tactics, techniques, procedures, indicators of compromise, and capabilities. Conforming punctuation changes are made to redesignated subparagraphs (D) and (E), and redesignated subparagraph (F) is struck.

Section 2(2)–(3) redesignates existing paragraph (2) as paragraph (7) and inserts new paragraphs (2) through (6):

- Paragraph (2) authorizes the Secretary to carry out program activities through an Energy Threat Analysis Center, which may be established at one or more physical locations (discretionary authority).
- Paragraph (3) provides that provision of assistance or information is at the Secretary's sole and unreviewable discretion and creates no substantive or procedural right or benefit to similar assistance for any other entity.
- Paragraph (4) exempts the program from treatment as an advisory committee under chapter 10 of title 5, U.S. Code (FACA nonapplicability).
- Paragraph (5) deems information shared under the program voluntarily shared and exempt from disclosure under 5 U.S.C. 552 (FOIA) and comparable State, Tribal, or local disclosure law, and mandates withholding without discretion under 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3)(B).
- Paragraph (6) grants transaction authority—supplemental to existing authority—permitting the Secretary to enter into contracts, cooperative agreements, grants, and other transactions with public agencies, private organizations, and persons, and to establish pre-approved national security contracting mechanisms, model partnership agreements, and expedited review procedures to minimize delays.

Section 2(4) amends redesignated paragraph (7) to extend the authorization of appropriations, striking "2022 through 2026" and inserting "2027 through 2031." This is an authorization of appropriations, not an appropriation. The bill specifies no separate effective date.
